card.band: 8 h. A frontier agent gets the basic tag and attribute rules right but loses points on CSS parsing, extension and script rules, and error-ordering details. A weaker model stops at plain tag-whitelist checks. Buckets: tag rules, attributes, CSS, layout, document-level rules.
card.cheat: Hard-coding golden outputs fails because the hidden and mutated inputs are not shipped. The snapshot has no newer validator copy, no node_modules copy of the validator, and no network.
card.grading: Run the CLI on hidden HTML files with golden outputs from the upstream validator, plus generated mutations of the visible cases (attributes dropped, tags reordered) whose expected output comes from a sealed copy of the real validator. Compare error code, line and column exactly. Visible sample cases are shipped; the hidden count is not found yet and must be measured.
card.reference: The upstream validator engine, trimmed to the same module set (several thousand lines of JS). It scores 1 by construction on the golden outputs.
card.task: /app ships a history-less snapshot with the validator engine (tag/attribute spec matching, CSS and URL checks, error reporting) removed. The agent rebuilds it as a Node CLI that reads an HTML file and prints PASS or the error list in the upstream text format. The protoascii rules file stays as input.

facts.claim: ampproject/amphtml exists at commit 3961d2e with a validator/ directory containing cpp/, js/, testdata/, validator-main.protoascii, validator-css.protoascii, validator-svg.protoascii, and build files (package.json, build.py, BUILD, WORKSPACE)

Engine sources include validator.h, validator-internal.cc, validator-convert.cc, parse-layout, parse-layout-sizes, parse-srcset, parse-viewport, error-formatter, keyframes-parse-css, type-identifier, utf8-util, plus nine *_test.cc unit tests

spike_plan.kill_if: Bazel build needs network beyond vendored deps and cannot be made offline, or outputs are nondeterministic across runs, or the reference is far above 10k lines so no 8h trial can reach 0.9.
spike_plan.pass_if: Engine builds offline from a clean Bazel cache or from vendored deps; at least 45 of 48 feature-test outputs reproduce exactly across three runs; engine size is measured and at least 150 changed lines are plausible for the chosen scope.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone ampproject/amphtml at 3961d2e and check out validator/.

Run the engine build from validator/cpp/engine per README (bazel build --cxxopt=-std=c++17 validator); record whether external WORKSPACE deps need network and whether the build succeeds from a clean cache.
Build the validator binary or wasm, then run it on all testdata/feature_tests/*.html and compare output with the matching .out files; record match count out of 48.
Run the same comparison three times to check determinism of output and error ordering.
Run wc -l on cpp/engine *.cc and *.h and on validator-main.protoascii to measure the reference size and correct the seed's JS line claim.
Count total files in testdata/feature_tests and sibling dirs with a local clone to fix the visible sample count.
Confirm that npm amphtml-validator 1.0.38 contains a compiled engine (inspect package contents) to decide the seal removal list.

v1.summary: The AMP validator is real, Apache-2.0, and pinned at 3961d2e, but the seed's reference is wrong: the engine is C++ under validator/cpp/engine (Bazel, C++17), not several thousand lines of JS, and the smoke probe is amber with no test suite, so reference build cost is unverified. Recommend a spike before committing, and narrowing scope to AMP HTML tag, attribute and document rules (dropping CSS, layout and srcset) so an 8h frontier trial can reach a meaningful share of the reference.
